Separate fresh human Decline and Cancel actions both returned ELICITATION_DENIED and minted no grant. The redacted receipt binds source a46beb73472c2e480c0a2a9bd2bde9abe8d64d4b and candidate SHA-256 e48a63ca218e73a5cc0cda31fa6e28cc46b89812fa6bf26b1532fc39b9a88564; no OAuth key/token, requestState, grant id, raw tool arguments or raw UI screenshot is stored. This accepts D5A only: public exec_command/apply_patch authority remains pre-cutover pending the complete real-target A4 corpus.

MTM-014 D5 resource hardening bounds pending consent to 256 global/32 per owner and retained grants to 2048 global/256 per owner, with on-issuance expired-record pruning, byte-bounded bindings/reasons and no live eviction or new workers. All 33 permission unit tests, six evidence-validator tests, 13 real OAuth/MCP capacity checks and the existing 22 MRTR checks pass. This is A3 with scripted consent only; independent human client evidence, complete target A4 and production cutover remain pending. The operator runbook is docs/MTM-014-D5-HUMAN-ACCEPTANCE.md.

MTM-013 is completed and stable MTM 0.4.0 remains the active release. Exact-binary loopback OAuth/MCP semantic regressions now bind the installed SHA-256 3312ca75a1de8707e740963cc0add4b09430dccc9dc63a3145e4456ff2b0cdf3: the QC constituent-matching case completed the full protocol-3 flow through direct_proving and the sigma-Hermitian case completed the compact lane; both reached done with server-computed correct verdict, passed LaTeX/finalizer gates and exported proof_verified.tex. The earlier preview.3 web-model runs remain historical supplemental evidence rather than being rewritten.

MTM-014 D1 is accepted in pre-authority shadow: Rust now has typed eight-kind Native permission, once/session scope and exec_command/apply_patch tool enums; validated permission requests retain no raw nested arguments and bind a canonical SHA-256 argument digest; safe/trusted/dangerous implicit Native profiles are typed data; and a shadow classifier exposes only permission dimensions already enforced by the accepted command policy. Production request_permissions, check_command_policy, Bubblewrap and workflow/finalizer authority are unchanged.

MTM-014 D2 is accepted in pre-authority shadow: RuntimeApplication now owns an empty process-local Native permission grant authority; explicit grants require an unforgeable VerifiedNativePermissionConsent with no public constructor, bind OAuth owner/workspace/tool/permission/argument digest/scope/expiry, atomically consume once grants, permit reusable session grants only inside the same process, fail closed on owner/workspace/tool/kind/argument/expiry/revocation mismatch, redact grant ids in Debug, and retain no raw command arguments. No production request_permissions, exec_command, apply_patch, Bubblewrap, workflow or finalizer path consumes these grants yet.

MTM-014 D3 is accepted in pre-authority shadow: complete typed exec/patch invocations bind the full canonical argument object, mode-neutral evaluation reports all seven exec risks in frozen order plus the generated-or-ignored patch risk, runtime collectors fail closed on executable/Git/path facts and metadata mutation, EffectiveNativePolicy is deterministic, and multi-risk ledger lookup consumes a complete one-shot set atomically without client grant ids. Pure explicit labels carry no authority without exact ledger grants. Production request_permissions, check_command_policy, exec_command, apply_patch, Bubblewrap, workflow and finalizer behavior remain unchanged.

MTM-014 D4 is accepted in pre-authority shadow: Bubblewrap compiles only a private-field validated SandboxPlan with fixed isolation invariants, while a private non-serializable PreparedPatch now separates no-write parsing, path/baseline preparation and Git authority facts from final authorization and rollback-capable commit. Dry runs neither authorize nor write; stale file, workspace, Git-ignore/config/include and symlink facts fail before authorization; concurrent prepared baselines have one winner; and failed multi-file commits roll back or retain recovery backups if restoration itself is obstructed. The stable public apply_patch path deliberately skips Git authority facts and preserves its successful result, empty/repeated path, move-over-existing and internal-source-symlink behavior until D5, so no explicit permission authority or production profile cutover occurred.

MTM-014 D5A selected MCP 2026-07-28 MRTR form elicitation and has now qualified that provider with a real MCP Inspector human UI. Legacy requests, modern requests without per-request form-elicitation capability, URL-only elicitation, OAuth authentication alone and model-generated confirmations remain non-authoritative. input_required requestState is a short-lived process-local opaque handle bound to OAuth owner, workspace and the exact typed permission request; production exec/apply_patch authority remains pre-cutover until complete real-target A4 acceptance.

MTM-014 D5A protocol plumbing is implemented: the gateway carries request-scoped modern client capabilities plus MRTR inputResponses/requestState outside public tool arguments, supports typed complete/input_required backend results, preserves input_required across modern result shaping, and returns the MCP missing-client-capability error -32021/HTTP 400 when a backend requests form elicitation from a client that did not declare it. Public tool schemas and legacy request shapes remain unchanged.

MTM-014 D5A has a process-local consent-challenge authority now connected only to request_permissions, not to exec_command/apply_patch enforcement. Each challenge is single-use, expires after 300 seconds, binds OAuth owner, workspace and the exact typed permission request, survives hostile owner/workspace/argument mismatches without being consumed, disappears on restart or expiry, redacts its opaque state from Debug, and exposes only a safe prompt plus argument fingerprint. accept+approved=true is the only completion that can construct VerifiedNativePermissionConsent; decline, cancel and approved=false construct no consent or grant.

MTM-014 D5A MRTR permission bridge now passes a 22-check real loopback OAuth/HTTP/MCP integration on the current debug binary. Modern form-capable safe requests can obtain input_required and mint a process-local exact grant only after accept+approved=true; a fresh duplicate exact request detects the active grant and does not prompt again, while stale requestState replay still fails closed. Argument mutation and extra input responses fail without consuming a still-valid challenge; decline mints no grant; legacy/no-capability behavior stays unsupported; trusted implicit permissions and non-intrinsic requests do not prompt; dangerous compatibility is preserved. This is protocol/authority integration evidence only, not independent human-UI evidence, and exec/apply_patch still do not consume grants.

MTM-014 D5 hardening now prevents normal grant issuance from creating overlapping active exact grants. The issuance mutex rejects a second owner/workspace/tool/permission/argument match even when its requested scope differs, while consumed once, expired and revoked grants no longer block replacement. The automatic authorization layer still rejects multiple active matches as ambiguous, with a dedicated legacy/corrupt-ledger test proving that defensive path consumes none.

MTM-014 now has an internal pre-cutover NativeAuthorityExecutor that is deliberately unreachable from public MCP dispatch and protected by a non-test dead-code tripwire. Its patch candidate passes exact once-grant, zero-write denial, dry-run, ordinary-path and argument-mutation tests; its command candidate passes safe isolated/shared network planning and a real Bubblewrap 0.9.0 once-grant execution test. Grant consumption occurs only after final fact revalidation and immediately before process start or patch mutation. D5A human consent is accepted, but public exec_command/apply_patch remain on the pre-cutover path until complete real-target A4 acceptance.

MTM-014 pre-cutover real-Bubblewrap qualification now covers all seven exec permission kinds on the candidate authority path: network, destructive_command, long_timeout, sensitive_env, shell_expansion, inline_script and privileged_executable. Git, pdfLaTeX and Sage also pass through the Dangerous auto-discovery candidate path. Magma is resolvable and launches in the candidate sandbox, but the current host Magma installation itself reports that it is not authorised, so Magma functional A4 remains explicitly blocked by the host license rather than being counted as an MTM pass or failure.

MTM-014 candidate lifecycle prequalification now directly passes TTY execution and stdin round-trip, bounded timeout, running-command termination, and descendant cleanup through the new authority seam while continuing to use the accepted CommandManager. A target-only candidate test also passes real public DNS plus HTTPS through a verified once network grant; that test is ignored by ordinary cargo test and must be invoked explicitly by the A4 target runner, so routine local gates never depend on external network availability.

MTM-014 pre-cutover permission-path target coverage now directly proves session-grant reuse and restart invalidation, cross-owner and cross-workspace non-consumption, trusted implicit-vs-explicit boundaries, dangerous complete Native implicit grants without workflow/vault inheritance, the 30,000/30,001 ms long-timeout boundary, and exact sensitive-environment argument binding on the real Bubblewrap candidate seam. Public exec_command/apply_patch dispatch is still unchanged; these checks qualify the candidate before authority cutover rather than exercising production through an unaccepted path.

MTM-014 target coverage now also drives a multi-risk InlineScript+LongTimeout invocation through the real candidate seam: one missing grant consumes none, adding the missing grant succeeds, and two concurrent invocations over a fresh pair of once grants produce exactly one full execution winner. A separate candidate patch test initializes a real Git repository, classifies an actually ignored path, denies it with zero writes before authorization, and commits it only after an exact once write_generated_or_ignored grant.

The hash-bound 22-check report proves safe/trusted/dangerous Bubblewrap isolation, real DNS/HTTPS, all candidate permission and grant boundaries, PreparedPatch/Git-ignore controls, TTY/stdin/timeout/kill/descendant cleanup, Git/pdfLaTeX/Sage non-regression, stable-selector preservation and workflow-authority non-inheritance.
